finding.claim: The ban endpoint catches the 403 raised by require_admin and carries on, so the admin check has no effect. Any authenticated non-admin can ban any user. abort(403) raises werkzeug's Forbidden, which subclasses Exception. The `except Exception` block only logs a warning and then falls through to do_ban(uid). The sibling unban endpoint calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is correctly protected. The inconsistency confirms the bug.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid. The user's g.user has no is_admin flag.
finding.sink: do_ban(uid), the privileged ban operation at admin.py:20

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST with an attacker-controlled uid
require_admin(g.user) is called; a non-admin hits abort(403) at admin.py:11, which raises Forbidden
except Exception catches the Forbidden HTTPException, so the 403 never reaches the client
The handler only logs a warning (it also logs the user's name, which is minor) and does not return or re-raise
do_ban(uid) executes for the non-admin, and the endpoint returns ok=True

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only guard, and it is neutralised by the broad except. There is no decorator, before_request hook or middleware in the file that enforces admin. The unban route at admin.py:26 does not swallow the exception, so it is not affected. Where g.user is populated is outside this file, so I did not review it. No other controls were found on the path.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19). That handler only logs and does not return or re-raise, so the check has no effect. The file has no before_request hook or decorator.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-19 the Forbidden raised by abort(403) at admin.py:11 is swallowed by `except Exception`, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any caller whose g.user lacks is_admin. The unban route at admin.py:26 calls require_admin without a try/except and is protected.
